posts.title: Broncos/Steelers Black Friday Discussion Thread
posts.description: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 22: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers #8 looks to throw during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Pittsburg Steelers on November 22nd, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Oh. We’re doing this again? Welcome back to BRB for Black Friday football, which is now a thing, I guess. Today, the Denver Broncos battle the post-Thanksgiving travel rush to get to the Steel City to play the Pittsburgh Steelers. You know that Black Friday deals are largely not deals, right? I mean I’m glad nobody’s getting trampled to death for a big screen TV anymore, but let’s not pretend you’re getting any kind of real savings on these sales? posts.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans takes the field prior to the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Reliant Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images I should start by addressing the first obvious question. Yes, Jacob and I are related. One of the few certain things in life is that when I run into a Barzilla, they have to be a relative. In this case, his grandfather and my father are first cousins. I think that makes me a second cousin once removed or some such technical mumbo jumbo. We will just say we are cousins and leave it at that. So, when I saw his name come across my feed as a Texans analysit I was more than a little curious. If you have downloaded the app, you have seen his analysis posted more than once. posts.title: Thanksgiving Day Triple-Header Discussion Thread
posts.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 22: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions plays against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field on November 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello, and from all of us here at Battle Red Blog, we’d like to wish you and yours a very happy Thanksgiving. But is it a happy Thanksgiving in terms of quality football? I’d almost say yes. We have three, count ‘em three games for your amusement and eventual post-fourth-piece-of-pie-background-nap-noise. In the opening salvo, hailing from the NFC North, it’s the Detroit Lions annual Turkey Day game and this one might actually be good! We have the 8-2 Detroit Lions hosting the also 8-2 Chicago Bears in a game with legitimate playoff seeding stakes on the line. It doesn’t get much more important than that. And then you have to take a nap while you get over how much you gorged yourself on food and football during the Lions game. That’s where the Cowboys and Eagles come in
